summary.text: The simplified character 备 means “prepare” or “ready.” Its traditional counterpart 備 is analyzed as 人, a person, with 𤰈, an arrow container or quiver, suggesting someone equipped and ready. Another analysis treats the whole graph as a quiver picture. 備 was also used in a bronze inscription for 箙, “quiver”; this may be a sound-based reuse of the sign, though the pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are not known.

formation.text: 備 has a disputed analysis. In one, 人 depicts a person and 𤰈 depicts arrows in a container; together they suggest someone carrying a quiver and being prepared. The received analysis also assigns 𤰈 a phonetic role, but the historical sound link has not been verified. Another interpretation treats the whole graph as a picture of a quiver. 备 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 備.

components.text: Within one analysis of 備, 人 depicts the person carrying the arrow container. Another interpretation treats the whole graph as a quiver picture, so this component breakdown is disputed.

In 備, 𤰈 is interpreted as arrows in a container, or a quiver. It is also assigned a phonetic role in one analysis, but the pictured object’s original name and pronunciation are not independently recovered.

sound_limitation.text: Modern Mandarin lists 𤰈 and 備 with the same reading, bèi. This match does not establish their historical sound relation, and the pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are not recovered.

sound.text: Both 𤰈 and 備 are listed with the modern Mandarin reading bèi. This current match does not establish that 𤰈 supplied 備’s historical sound.

history.text: 備 is reported in oracle-bone, bronze, and manuscript script categories, but the earliest appearance and sequence among those categories are unresolved.

The modern printed right-hand form 𤰇 is described as a change from seal-script 𤰈. Some bronze forms also change the lower part of 𤰈 to 用, tentatively treated as a sound element; these descriptions do not establish a dated sequence.
In 1956, 备 was standardized as the simplified counterpart of 備. 俻 is documented as a variant of 備, but its specific role in the formation of 备 is unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The carrying-quiver interpretation may explain the graph’s association with readiness, but does not establish the spoken word’s earliest meaning. 備 is reported in a bronze inscription as a written sign for 箙, “quiver”; this may reflect reuse because the words sounded similar, but the pictured container’s original name and pronunciation are not recovered.

Reported meanings include prepared or complete, for use, cautious, equipment, and all or entirely. The cited examples do not establish a complete chronology or continuous development among these senses.

senses.text: Bronze uses are reported with glosses such as “equipped” or “complete” and “for use.” The carrying-quiver interpretation may help explain preparedness, but does not prove this was the word’s earliest spoken sense.

senses.period: received lexicographic tradition; date of spoken sense unresolved
senses.text: The received dictionary gloss includes “cautious” or “careful”; this does not establish the earliest spoken meaning.
Dictionary citations include uses glossed “all” or “entirely,” but do not establish when this sense arose or how it relates chronologically to preparation or completeness.
Later cited examples use 備 for equipment or facilities. The evidence does not establish that this meaning followed a particular earlier sense.

limitations.text: The earliest attested spoken sense is unresolved. Reported bronze contexts and received dictionary glosses do not provide a complete dated history of the meanings.
A bronze inscription reportedly reuses 備 as a written sign for 箙, “quiver.” The proposed sound-based borrowing does not verify that 箙 sounded like the pictured container’s unrecovered original name.

The forms for 備 are described as oracle-bone, bronze, and seal script, but their shapes cannot be compared here to verify which features are visible in each candidate. The quiver interpretation therefore cannot be tied to a specific glyph image.

overview.text: Today, 备 means “prepare” or “ready.” Its traditional counterpart 備 is analyzed as a person carrying an arrow container, suggesting readiness. 備 was also used for 箙 (“quiver”) in a bronze inscription, possibly because the words sounded alike; the pictured container’s original name is not known.
